Hi Samira — thanks for the sample and the great conversation. I'm including Ben (Customer Success) and Jonas (Solutions Engineering) to own the technical and scoring work.

Recap & proposed trial split (high level):

1) Phase 0 (prep, 1 week) — data access, schema alignment, privacy review, SOC2 evidence request. Owners: Priya + Jonas.
2) Phase 1 (offline eval, 2 weeks) — run the sample and an extended offline dataset through Redwood's batch grading harness. Purpose: measure base accuracy, safety-filter false positives, and tune prompts/filters. Deliverable: eval report + recommended thresholds. Owner: Jonas.
3) Phase 2 (shadow, 3 weeks) — run in shadow mode against a small percentage of live traffic (5–10%) to measure production behavior and latency under realistic conditions. This is where we'll observe KV cache effectiveness and routing behavior. Owner: Ben.
4) Phase 3 (live pilot, 2 weeks) — Optional short live pilot if acceptance gates are met.

Proposed acceptance gates (examples — we'll refine with your team):
- Accuracy: weighted precision >= 86% on core triage intents (offline rubric)
- Safety: downstream safety-rule false positive rate <= 1%
- Latency: P95 end-to-end generation + routing <= 850ms for <512 tokens (US region)
- Cost guardrails: projected token cost per 1k ops within agreed budget band
- Observability: tracing and token-level logs available for audit window

Owners & next steps:
- Priya (AM): program lead, weekly syncs, contract/terms touchpoints
- Jonas (SE): runs offline eval and creates eval-rubric.xlsx; handles dataset ingestion
- Ben (CS): coordinates shadow runbooks and success gating during live traffic
Attachments: trial-charter-v1.pdf, eval-rubric.xlsx

2) Confirm who on your side will own compliance questions (we'll need a SOC2 point-of-contact).
3) Are you ok with the 5–10% traffic slice for shadow (we can adjust down if needed)?

Quick note on the grading rubric and shadow duration.

Priya — thanks for the clear split. A couple suggestions from CS lens:
- Grading buckets: instead of a single threshold, use a 3-tier acceptance band per intent: Green (>=90%), Yellow (80–89%), Red (<80%). For yellow, we define remediation actions (prompt tweaks, filter rules) and re-run the offline eval.
- Safety gating should be binary (pass/fail) for high-risk intents — if any message triggers a safety rule in offline tests above the tolerance, we fail the gate until remediated.
- Shadow duration: 3 weeks is fine for behavioral sampling, but given HealthSpark's regulated domain, propose we do a 1-week focused shadow first (very low volume, strict logging), then extend to 2 more weeks if both sides are comfortable. This reduces risk and gets faster feedback.

Example acceptance rubric snippet (to include in eval-rubric.xlsx):
- Intent accuracy (weighted): Green >=90 (3 pts), Yellow 80–89 (2 pts), Red <80 (0 pts)
- P95 latency: Green <=700ms (3 pts), Yellow 700–850ms (2 pts), Red >850ms (0 pts)
- Safety violations per 10k messages: Green 0 (3 pts), Yellow 0–1 (2 pts), Red >1 (0 pts)

We'll make these editable in the spreadsheet so HealthSpark can set the weights. Jonas — can you confirm the data schema we need for scoring (fields + sample mapping)?

Ben
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
